newsitem.title: USA: Investor demand for Rite Aid debt issue grows.
newsitem.headline: Investor demand for Rite Aid debt issue grows.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp's multi-tranche debt offering was boosted in size to $1.0 billion as corporate bond underwriters struggled to meet investor demand for the paper, syndicate sources said.
"The deal was boosted to $1.0 billion to meet strong demand for the paper," one high-grade syndicate source said.
The initial size of the three-part offering was set at $600 million, sources added.
The first tranche, $350 million in five-year debt is expected to price at a spread of 50 to 55 basis points over Treasuries.
The second Rite Aid tranche, $350 million in 10-year debt is expected to price between 70 to 75 basis points over Treasuries.
The final tranche, $300 million in 30-year debt is expected to price at a spread of 100 to 105 basis points.
The deal, which is expected to price via Goldman Sachs & Co later today is rated A3/BBB-plus, sources said.
Goldman Sachs & Co is the lead manager on the deal with JP Morgan Securities, Bear Stearns and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette as co-underwriters for the offering.
Among other investment grade offerings, Scholastic Corp is expected to issue $125 million in seven-year notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Also, American Re Corp is expected to tap the market with $500 million in 30-year noncallable 144A debt also via Goldman Sachs & Co. The deal is expected to be rated Aa1/AA.

Meanwhile, dealers said with not much left to the calendar year and the Christmas and New Year's holidays approaching the bulk of supply is likely to come this week while desks are still fully staffed.
Among upcoming high-yield debt offerings the following are expected, dealers said.
- Wilshire Financial Services Group Inc's $75 million in seven-year notes.
- Maxxam Group Holdings' $100 million in 144A notes due 2003 via Bear Stearns & Co. Price talk on the issue is 10.75 to 12.0 percent.
- Mechala Group Jamaica Ltd's JAM.N $75 million in three-year 144A notes.
- Willcox & Gibbs' $85 million in seven-year 144A notes via Dillon Read & Co.
Among Monday's high-yield issuers Heartland Wireless Communications Inc issued $125 million in notes due 2004 to yield 14.0 percent.
TV Filme set $140 million in senior notes due 2004 to yield 12.875 percent.
And, Lodgenet Entertainment's $150 million in 144A senior unsecured notes due 2006 which priced to yield 10.25 percent.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is off 21/32 at 97-22/32 to yield 6.68 percent compared with Monday's 6.62 percent at the close.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
